keyQuotes: Everyone saw the numerical contrast. ... This article tries to explain another question: why is the price still rising when everyone thinks it's expensive?
No one is crazy. It's just that the rational behavior of all individuals combined has produced a seemingly crazy price.
In Soros's terms of 'reflexivity,' market prices do not merely reflect fundamentals; they may also change fundamentals in return.

mainPoints.explanation: Limited supply of Coding Plan on the product side, an extremely low free float on the capital side, coupled with passive allocation triggered by inclusion in the Hang Seng Tech Index, create a self-reinforcing cycle of excess demand.
mainPoints.point: The core driver of Zhipu's trillion valuation is not fundamentals, but scarcity.

mainPoints.explanation: Market prices not only fail to reflect fundamentals, but can also change fundamentals by influencing financing, talent, and customer resources. As long as the cycle remains unbroken, calling it expensive cannot stop the price from rising.
mainPoints.point: The reflexivity theory explains how bubbles form and persist.

mainPoints.explanation: If competitors like DeepSeek release models with comparable performance that are more open, Zhipu's scarcity will disappear, and pricing power will shift accordingly.
mainPoints.point: The real risk Zhipu faces is the loss of its competitive advantage.

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the market logic behind Zhipu's trillion-HKD valuation: driven by scarcity, passive allocation, and narrative premium, while noting that roughly half of the valuation comes from real growth and the other half from structural amplification.
dataList.originalTitle: 万亿智谱，凭什么？
dataList.summary: Taking Zhipu's market cap surpassing one trillion HKD as a starting point, the article analyzes the company's 2025 financial report (revenue of 724 million yuan, net loss of 4.718 billion yuan, R&D expenditure of 3.18 billion yuan) and the technical performance of its GLM-5.2 model to explain why the market continues to push the stock price higher despite the clearly excessive valuation. The author identifies three underlying logics: a dual scarcity effect formed by the limited supply of Coding Plan on the product side and an extremely low free float (only about 2.67% of H-shares are tradable) on the capital side; concentrated passive buying triggered by inclusion in the Hang Seng Tech Index; and the scarcity narrative around foundational AI model companies. The article also references Keynes's beauty contest theory and Soros's reflexivity concept to analyze how prices become self-reinforcing. It warns of risks: the unlocking of restricted shares in July and slowing quarterly growth could lead to a valuation collapse, as well as potential competitive threats from DeepSeek and others. Finally, it points out that the risk-reward ratio at current prices is severely asymmetric, and whether Zhipu can transform its high valuation into an infrastructure platform position will be the key to long-term success.
dataList.title: What Justifies Zhipu's Trillion Valuation?

mainPoints.point: Foundational skills (collaboration, mathematical thinking, adaptability) determine long-term career ceilings more than specialized technical skills.

mainPoints.explanation: Since 2007, the proportion of management job descriptions emphasizing collaboration, coaching, and influence has tripled; jobs combining cognitive abilities with social skills command the highest wage premiums.
mainPoints.point: Social skills are the glue for efficient team collaboration, and the related demand continues to grow.

mainPoints.point: Enterprises should prioritize foundational skills in hiring and development, rather than focusing solely on specialized knowledge.

mainPoints.point: Managers can reinforce foundational skills through daily behavioral modeling and system design.

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: Based on a large-scale study covering 70 million job transitions, this article demonstrates that in an era of shrinking technology half-lives, foundational skills such as collaboration, mathematical thinking, and adaptability are more decisive of long-term career ceilings and organizational adaptability than specialized technical skills.
dataList.originalTitle: 未来五年，比技术更值钱的是这些基础能力
dataList.summary: Based on large-scale data from over 70 million job transitions across more than 1,000 occupations in the United States between 2005 and 2019, the article categorizes skills into foundational skills (reading comprehension, basic math, teamwork) and specialized advanced skills (such as blockchain). The study finds that individuals with higher foundational skill scores earn higher wages throughout their careers, get promoted faster, learn new skills more quickly, and adapt better to industry changes. The article provides three specific recommendations for leaders: prioritize screening candidates with strong foundational skills during hiring; invest in early-career development to strengthen soft skills; and have managers lead by example to model and reward foundational skill behaviors.
dataList.title: In the Next Five Years, These Foundational Skills Will Be More Valuable Than Technical Skills

keyQuotes: DSpark pairs a parallel draft backbone with a tiny sequential head to cut suffix decay.
In production on DeepSeek-V4, per-user generation runs 60–85% faster than the MTP-1 baseline.

mainPoints.explanation: The parallel backbone (DFlash) provides base logits, and a tiny sequential head adds prefix-dependent bias, cutting suffix decay without costly autoregression.
mainPoints.point: DSpark uses a semi-autoregressive draft backbone: parallel base with a cheap Markov head to sustain acceptance across the block.

mainPoints.explanation: The confidence head estimates per-token acceptance probability (calibrated via Sequential Temperature Scaling), and the scheduler uses a profiled throughput curve to decide how many tokens to verify based on GPU load.
mainPoints.point: A confidence head and load-aware scheduler optimize verification budget per request.

mainPoints.explanation: At matched throughput, DSpark-5 configuration (5-token draft block with Markov head) accelerates generation for both Flash and Pro variants, with output lossless.
mainPoints.point: In production on DeepSeek-V4, DSpark achieves 60-85% per-user speedup over the MTP-1 baseline.

mainPoints.explanation: DeepSpec provides a three-stage pipeline (data preparation, training, evaluation) supporting multiple targets, and the draft module attaches to existing V4 weights without retraining the target.
mainPoints.point: The DSpark checkpoints and DeepSpec training code are open-sourced under MIT license.

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: DeepSeek releases DSpark, a speculative decoding framework that accelerates per-user generation by 60-85% on DeepSeek-V4 via semi-autoregressive drafting and load-aware scheduling.

dataList.summary: The article reports DeepSeek's open-source release of DSpark, a speculative decoding framework designed for production serving. It explains DSpark's semi-autoregressive draft mechanism combining a parallel backbone with a lightweight Markov head to maintain high acceptance deep into the block, and a confidence-scheduled verifier that dynamically adjusts verification length based on GPU load. Offline benchmarks show accepted length gains of 16-31% over DFlash and Eagle3. In production on DeepSeek-V4-Flash and V4-Pro, per-user generation speed improves 60-85% over the MTP-1 baseline, with lossless output. The release includes checkpoints and the MIT-licensed DeepSpec training code.
dataList.title: DeepSeek Releases DSpark， a Speculative Decoding Framework That Accelerates DeepSeek-V4 Per-User Generation 60–85% Over MTP-1

keyQuotes: The fix is not 'a better algorithm.' It is the simplest of all: bookkeeping.
Book before you build. Always.
Failure that explains itself is the most beautiful thing.
Same animal in a new zoo.

mainPoints.explanation: Each process reserves VRAM for the full context window (e.g., 6.5 GB for Llama 1B with large context), leaving insufficient space for other processes. The OOM is caused by KV cache reservation, not the model itself.
mainPoints.point: Multiple llama-completion processes fail in parallel due to upfront KV cache pre-allocation, not model weights.

mainPoints.explanation: The daemon maintains a ledger of allocated bytes and admits a new agent only if current usage plus estimated need stays under a configurable cap (e.g., 90%). This prevents OOM at registration time.
mainPoints.point: A VRAM ledger with simple admission control solves the overcommitment problem.

mainPoints.explanation: If you load the model first and check budget second, you waste I/O and risk races. The daemon reserves VRAM in the ledger before any GGUF is loaded, and rolls back on failure, leaving no trace.
mainPoints.point: The order of operations matters: book (reserve in ledger) before build (load model).

mainPoints.explanation: By initializing llama_backend once and sharing a refcounted model map, the daemon reuses weights and avoids hundreds of megabytes of per-process driver overhead.
mainPoints.point: Sharing a single llama backend avoids redundant CUDA context overhead.

mainPoints.explanation: Just as a base station decides whether to admit a new call without degrading existing ones, the daemon rejects new agents before they load if they would exceed VRAM capacity, with clear error codes.
mainPoints.point: The problem mirrors Connection Admission Control (CAC) in cellular networks.

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: This article explains why running multiple LLM-based agents in parallel on a single low-VRAM GPU fails due to KV cache pre-allocation, and presents a small C++ daemon (lmxd) that enforces VRAM bookkeeping to solve the problem.
dataList.originalTitle: 3 Agents. 3 LLMs. 1 Aging GPU: Engineering Parallel Inference on Bare Metal
dataList.summary: The article addresses the practical challenge of running three AI agents, each using a different small LLM, on a single GTX 1080 with only 8 GB VRAM. The naive approach of launching separate llama-completion processes fails because each process pre-reserves a large KV cache for the full context window, causing the second and third processes to OOM. The author introduces lmxd, a ~1500-line C++ daemon that acts as a VRAM bookkeeper. Agents communicate with the daemon over a Unix socket using a simple text protocol (REGISTER, DECODE, etc.). The daemon maintains a ledger that enforces a 90% VRAM cap, admits new agents only if the estimated memory fits, and loads models in a shared backend to avoid redundant CUDA context overhead. The article provides detailed code snippets, explains the critical order of operations (book before build), and presents benchmark results on the same hardware, showing that the daemon successfully admits all three agents where the naive approach admits only one. It also covers KV-swap mechanisms for time-slicing decode across agents, and draws an insightful analogy to Connection Admission Control (CAC) in cellular networks.
dataList.title: 3 Agents. 3 LLMs. 1 Aging GPU: Engineering Parallel Inference on Bare Metal

keyQuotes: More than half of Notion Mail users manage email without ever opening their inbox.
The future of software lies in completing work for users, not just displaying work content.

mainPoints.explanation: The core reason for Notion Mail's closure is a shift in user behavior—over half of users manage email through Agents without opening their inboxes. Notion believes the future of software is completing work for users rather than displaying work content, leading to a decisive pivot.
mainPoints.point: Notion abandons the email client, pivoting to fully Agent-managed inboxes.

mainPoints.explanation: Product leadership explained that Notion Calendar is retained because time information inherently requires a visual interface, while email is text that can exist in forms like chat or databases, without needing a dedicated inbox. This judgment reflects an essential distinction between the two product categories.
mainPoints.point: Calendars need GUIs; email can be consumed by Agents.

mainPoints.explanation: A new generation of products (such as AgentMail, QQ Mail Agent Mail) designs email services specifically for Agents, with Agents having independent accounts and API interfaces, decoupled from human interfaces. This marks a shift in the email category from enhancing human experience to building machine communication infrastructure.
mainPoints.point: "Mail for AI" is replacing "AI Mail," as Agents need independent communication identities.

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: Notion announced the closure of Notion Mail, its AI email client launched just 14 months ago, pivoting toward fully Agent-managed inboxes—a decision that reflects a fundamental shift in the AI email space from feature-stacking that optimizes user experience to building independent communication infrastructure for AI Agents.
dataList.originalTitle: 上线 14 个月，Notion 关掉了自己的 AI 邮件产品
dataList.summary: This article reports that Notion will fully shut down Notion Mail on September 22, 2026, with the product lasting only 17 months from launch to closure. The piece traces Notion Mail's origins—the acquisition of Skiff, aimed at challenging Google Workspace, with deep AI integration at its core (natural language labeling, automated email handling, etc.). The article maintains a clear stance, combining factual reporting with independent judgment, offering valuable insight into AI product trends.

keyQuotes: The agentic platform defines what needs to be provided. Team Topologies defines who provides it, and how teams interact to make it happen.
Cognitive load does not disappear with AI --- it transforms. It first becomes an anticipation burden: everything the human must foresee before launching the agent, or the output will fall short.
The developer does not disappear: they shift. They no longer produce the application --- they build the platform that enables others to produce it.

mainPoints.explanation: Where human roles once spread complexity over time, agents produce instantly. The human must foresee all questions upfront, creating a throughput problem the platform must absorb.
mainPoints.point: Cognitive load in agentic production compresses from sequential roles to an anticipation burden on a single person.

mainPoints.explanation: The platform guarantees production reliability (deployment, monitoring, systemic guardrails). Business teams focus on intent and dynamic context, not end-to-end operations.
mainPoints.point: Stream-aligned teams can be non-technical business teams because the platform absorbs operational and technical complexity.

mainPoints.explanation: Observable criteria include guardrail coverage, pipeline reliability, self-service share, documentation completeness, and audit trails. Without these, the platform cannot absorb operational responsibility.
mainPoints.point: The platform matures when guardrails are automatic, deployments are self-service, and decision traceability exists.

mainPoints.explanation: When three teams reinvent the same guardrail, it becomes a candidate for systemization. The platform product owner generalizes and documents it, preventing local reinvention and scaling reliability.
mainPoints.point: A graduation path (rule of three) ensures guardrails move from team-specific to platform-owned.

mainPoints.explanation: Centralized deployment, monitoring, and usage metrics give systemic visibility. The platform's product owner tracks active applications, flags those that fail security checks, and triggers deprecation.
mainPoints.point: Ease of production must be matched by ease of oversight to prevent shadow IT.

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: This article applies Team Topologies to the agentic platform, defining team types and interactions to distribute the transformed cognitive load of AI-driven production.
dataList.originalTitle: Who Does What? Team Topologies for the Agentic Platform
dataList.summary: The article extends Team Topologies (Skelton & Pais) to the context of AI agents producing applications. It argues that cognitive load in agentic production does not disappear but compresses onto a single person, becoming an "anticipation burden" and "cognitive throughput" problem. The agentic platform absorbs part of this burden by making itself queryable by agents. The author adapts the four team types: stream-aligned teams become non-technical business teams; the platform team provides systemic context, guardrails, and tooling as self-service; enabling teams temporarily bridge gaps; complicated subsystem teams handle deep AI infrastructure. Three interaction modes—facilitating, X-as-a-Service, collaboration—evolve as teams and platform mature. Governance (shadow IT prevention) and a graduation path (rule of three for guardrail systemization) are proposed to make the model sustainable. The article concludes that business teams can become stream-aligned without coding, as the platform absorbs technical complexity, while developers shift to building the platform.
dataList.title: Who Does What? Team Topologies for the Agentic Platform

keyQuotes: Diagnostic logs can exist, but they must have clear levels, sampling, sanitization, retention, and size boundaries.
Debugging information can be abundant, but what is persisted by default must be minimal, stable, explainable, and controllable.
Stopping the bleeding can be done with a trigger, `sqlite_home` migration, or WAL cleanup. Curing the disease can only happen within Codex's own SQLite log sink.

mainPoints.explanation: Even with `RUST_LOG=warn` set, this sink has an independent filter chain, causing high-frequency noise such as WebSocket/SSE payloads to be persistently written to disk.
mainPoints.point: Codex's SQLite log sink defaults to allowing TRACE-level logs from all targets, leading to massive amounts of useless data being written to disk.

mainPoints.explanation: After inserting a new row, index updates and old row deletions are triggered, resulting in actual SSD writes far exceeding the net file growth. Extrapolated yearly writes can reach 640 TB.
mainPoints.point: SQLite's WAL mode and insert-prune cycle cause the file size to remain stable while the underlying write volume is enormous.

mainPoints.explanation: The trigger sacrifices feedback logs and is not a long-term solution; macOS's /tmp is not a ramdisk, making symlinks ineffective. The correct approach is to use `sqlite_home` to migrate to an external drive or wait for an upstream fix.
mainPoints.point: The popular online mitigations—trigger blocking and symlinking to /tmp—each have serious limitations.

mainPoints.explanation: This includes setting a stricter default filter level, sanitizing payloads, adding a global size cap, and a configuration toggle. Users should not rely on workarounds.
mainPoints.point: Upstream fixes should focus on boundary control for persistent logs.

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the SSD write amplification issue caused by the OpenAI Codex logging system writing heavily at TRACE level to SQLite, presenting a chain of evidence, risk stratification, immediate mitigation measures, and upstream fix directions.
dataList.originalTitle: Codex 日志正在燃烧你的 SSD
dataList.summary: This article dissects the logging system issue in OpenAI Codex: its persistent SQLite log sink defaults to accepting TRACE-level logs from all targets, bypassing the user-set `RUST_LOG=warn` filter, leading to continuous high-frequency writes to `logs_2.sqlite` and its WAL file during streaming output. From the source code perspective, the article explains the write amplification mechanism (WAL mode, multiple indexes, insert-prune cycle), cites data from open issues on GitHub such as #17320 and #28224 (e.g., 5 MiB/s write rate, extrapolated 640 TB writes per year), and points out that the file size users see may differ dramatically from actual SSD write volume. The author stratifies the risks to avoid over-panicking, while emphasizing that Mac users face higher risk. The article evaluates three mitigation measures circulating online (SQLite trigger to block inserts, symlink to /tmp or a ramdisk, migrating the SQLite directory to an external drive), detailing their limitations and proper usage. Finally, it proposes the truly necessary upstream fixes: narrowing the default filter, sanitizing protocol payloads, and adding a global size cap. The article cites specific code lines and issue links, with rigorous reasoning and practical advice.
dataList.title: Codex Logs Are Burning Your SSD

keyQuotes: Money can't be created out of nowhere, so we can't tolerate duplicates or arbitrary balance updates.
No trust. Trust neither external providers, internal components, nor the world.
Rounding breaks sums. If a number is split into parts and rounding is applied, the sum of the parts might no longer equal the original number.

mainPoints.explanation: The handbook details four approaches: floating-point, arbitrary precision (BigDecimal), minor-units integer (e.g., cents, satoshis), and rational numbers, emphasizing that storage and computation can combine different methods.
mainPoints.point: Money representation must use precise types; floating-point is almost never acceptable.

mainPoints.explanation: Rounding should occur only at boundaries like persistence or display, and residuals must be tracked to avoid creating or losing money.
mainPoints.point: Rounding is a business decision with legal implications and must be explicit, conservative, and minimized.

mainPoints.explanation: Every transaction moves money between accounts (credit/debit), and the books always balance. External providers have dedicated accounts. Corrections are made via compensating entries, never by editing the original.
mainPoints.point: Double-entry bookkeeping ensures money is never created or destroyed; balance is derived from movements.

mainPoints.explanation: Event sourcing is the most principled approach, but comes with complexity. For non-money domains, a conventional model with reliable change logging may suffice.
mainPoints.point: Audit trails require immutable, append-only logs with full context: what, when, who, and why.

mainPoints.explanation: Financial records are largely exempt; PII can be stored in mutable stores keyed by opaque IDs, and encryption key deletion achieves erasure without rewriting history.
mainPoints.point: GDPR erasure can be reconciled with immutable ledgers by separating PII from financial data and using crypto-shredding.

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: This handbook provides a comprehensive set of engineering patterns for building trustworthy financial systems, covering money representation, ledger recording, and execution flows.
dataList.originalTitle: Fintech Engineering Handbook
dataList.summary: The Fintech Engineering Handbook is a living document aimed at software engineers building systems where money is the primary focus. It is structured around three core principles: no invented data, no lost data, and no trust. The handbook begins with representing money, covering precision handling (floating-point, arbitrary precision, minor-units, rational numbers), rounding strategies, currency handling (packaging amount and currency, no cross-currency arithmetic, controlled currency set), and FX rates (directionality, time, transactional vs reference rates). It then moves to recording money via the ledger, explaining double-entry bookkeeping, distinction between value time, booking time, and settlement time, audit trails, event sourcing, immutability, reversals and corrections, and GDPR considerations. Finally, it introduces executing money flows with invariants. The content is practical, with clear trade-offs and principles touched for each pattern.

keyQuotes: there exists a three-phase factual recall circuit within the Gemma model family
Facts are encoded as directions in the residual stream at the entity token. The residual stream dominates causally here, contributing 40× more than attention outputs and 18× more than MLP outputs.

I found that this three-phase circuit replicated at scale: storage shifted to layers 0–27, routing remained distributed with no significantly dominant head, and readout concentrated in the final layers, structurally identical to Gemma-2B, proportionally scaled
cross-model mechanistic comparisons are partly constrained by tokenizer-induced dataset drift, and reported differences should be interpreted with that caveat in mind

mainPoints.explanation: Storage happens in the residual stream at the entity token's position (layers 0–14 for 2B, 0–27 for 12B). Routing is distributed across attention heads with no single dominant head. Readout is a simple pass-through in the final layers.
mainPoints.point: Factual recall in Gemma follows a three-phase circuit: storage, routing, and readout.

mainPoints.explanation: In Gemma-2B, residual stream damage (ΔLD = -11.47) is 18x larger than MLP output damage and 40x larger than attention output damage, confirming facts are encoded as directions in the stream.
mainPoints.point: The residual stream dominates causal effect over individual sublayers in the storage phase.

mainPoints.explanation: Gemma-12B-IT shows the same structure proportionally: storage shifts to layers 0–27, routing remains distributed and even duller, and readout concentrates in the final layers.
mainPoints.point: The three-phase circuit replicates at scale from 2B to 12B parameters.

mainPoints.explanation: Even models sharing the same tokenizer (SentencePiece) can map some words to different token IDs (e.g., 'hertz' as two tokens), causing prompt pair exclusion in larger models and requiring upfront token run checks.
mainPoints.point: Tokenizer differences introduce dataset drift that constrains cross-model comparisons.

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: This paper presents a mechanistic interpretability study localizing a three-phase factual recall circuit (storage, routing, readout) in Gemma-2B and Gemma-12B-IT via activation patching, with the circuit scaling proportionally across model sizes.
dataList.originalTitle: A Three-Phase Factual Recall Circuit in Gemma-2B and Gemma-12B-IT
dataList.summary: The author designs a battery of 60 clean/corrupt prompt pairs across 20 fact categories and uses activation patching with TransformerLens to isolate factual recall circuits in Gemma-2B and Gemma-12B-IT. A novel metric called TotalSwing is introduced to rank prompt pairs by signal strength. Four experiments progressively narrow down from full residual stream to individual attention heads. Results reveal a consistent three-phase circuit: (1) Storage in the residual stream at the entity token position (layers 0-14 in 2B, 0-27 in 12B), (2) Distributed routing via attention heads (no single dominant head), and (3) Readout as a pass-through in the final layers (layers 15-17 in 2B, proportionally in 12B). The circuit replicates at scale, but tokenizer differences cause dataset drift between models, a caveat for cross-model comparisons. The author discusses future work including path patching and SAE analysis, constrained by disk space limitations. The full codebase is open-sourced.
dataList.title: A Three-Phase Factual Recall Circuit in Gemma-2B and Gemma-12B-IT

dataList.oneSentenceSummary: This article shares Delivery Hero's journey of replacing Google Analytics with an internal user tracking service, achieving higher data quality (97% vs 85%), 3x cost savings, and 10x load increase through careful architecture, testing, and incremental optimization.
dataList.originalTitle: Challenging Google Analytics: Building a Scalable， Cost-Effective User Tracking Service
dataList.summary: The article presents a detailed talk by Alina Krasavina, an engineering manager at Delivery Hero, on building and scaling an internal user tracking service (Perseus) to replace Google Analytics. It covers the motivations: migration necessity, real-time data needs, GDPR compliance, and cost control. The initial MVP used a simple API with Pub/Sub processors, which proved highly scalable. The rollout involved parallel testing with a double pipeline (sending data to both GA and internal service), progressive rollout across brands, and load testing with 3x peak traffic. After rollout, data quality improved from 85% to 97% (measured by order match rate), and cost dropped to 25% less than GA, later to 3x cheaper. Post-MVP challenges included data completeness (null standardization), backend reliability (pod restart data loss solved by synchronous requests and retries), and further cost optimizations (data archiving, JSON storage, cheaper nodes). SDK improvements like event prioritization, non-blocking queuing, and monitoring helped prevent data loss during A/B tests. A key innovation was code-generated event models that enforce data quality at compile time, reducing governance overhead. The talk emphasizes the value of a simplistic initial architecture, careful KPI selection, thorough testing, and incremental improvements.
dataList.title: Challenging Google Analytics: Building a Scalable， Cost-Effective User Tracking Service
